title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent U.S. economic data and Federal Reserve communications have produced a closely divided trader consensus on the September 2026 FOMC decision, with no change priced at 56.5% and a 25 basis point hike at 42.5%.** Elevated inflation—driven by energy prices tied to Middle East supply disruptions—has kept core PCE readings above the 2% target and prompted hawkish signals, including three dissents favoring a hike at the July meeting and dot-plot projections showing several officials expecting at least one increase by year-end. Counterbalancing this, July payrolls contracted modestly and the unemployment rate held near 4.1%, signaling a cooling labor market that reduces immediate pressure for tightening. Incoming August employment and inflation figures, due shortly before the September 15-16 meeting, remain the primary near-term catalysts that could shift the balance between these two leading outcomes.

title: 2026 Men’s US Open Winner (Tennis)
description:
The 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament is scheduled for August 23 - September 13, 2026.

This market will resolve to the player that wins the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed player to win the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament per the rules of the tournament, the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament is cancelled, postponed after October 31, 2026, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Open (https://www.usopen.org/index.html); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Carlos Alcaraz leads the 2026 US Open winner market at 42.5% implied probability as the defending champion returning from a four-month right wrist injury layoff. Jannik Sinner’s pre-tournament withdrawal with a knee injury and Novak Djokovic’s first-round upset loss to Mariano Navone have opened the draw, elevating Alcaraz despite limited match play and his straight-sets opener against Roman Safiullin. Alexander Zverev sits second at 21.3% after claiming the 2026 French Open title and reaching the Wimbledon final, though he survived a five-set first-round test against Lorenzo Sonego and enters with mixed hard-court results. Taylor Fritz and Ben Shelton follow around 10%, supported by home-court form and recent results, while the remaining field trails as underdogs in a tournament where recent major pedigree and fitness now define trader consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description: The fragmented Democratic field remains wide open two years before the 2028 primaries, with prediction market traders pricing in a competitive contest shaped by polling volatility and party debates over progressive versus moderate messaging. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez holds the top spot at 20 percent amid gains in early-state surveys like New Hampshire and strong small-dollar fundraising among the party's left wing, while Jon Ossoff at 15.8 percent benefits from viral Senate reelection visibility and perceived crossover appeal in Georgia despite repeated denials of interest. Gavin Newsom at 14.1 percent has seen earlier leads erode amid scrutiny of his record, as Kamala Harris and others trail further behind. The 2026 midterms and finalized primary calendar with South Carolina first could clarify lanes before major announcements.

title: Elon Musk # tweets August 28 - September 4, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from August 28 12:00 PM ET to September 4, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Marine Le Pen’s July 2026 court ruling, which upheld her embezzlement conviction but shortened the ineligibility period enough for her to run, combined with her immediate candidacy announcement, has anchored her at the front of first-round polling around 34-36%. Édouard Philippe has consolidated as the leading centrist alternative, regularly polling in the mid-teens to low 20s and positioned to draw from both former Macron supporters and moderate right voters. Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s recent gains to the mid-teens reflect left-wing consolidation efforts, yet the broader field remains splintered across figures such as Gabriel Attal, Raphaël Glucksmann, and Bruno Retailleau. This fragmentation sustains tight implied probabilities between Le Pen and Philippe, as traders weigh the historical tendency for anti-RN voters to coalesce in any runoff against the risk that persistent division prevents any single challenger from securing the second spot. Upcoming events including further legal appeals and primary processes could shift positioning before the April 2027 first round.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Milwaukee Brewers enter the series with an MLB-best 87-53 record and a nine-game lead in the NL Central over the 78-62 Cubs, fueled by elite pitching depth and a .340 on-base percentage. Jackson Chourio's recent power surge, including a four-hit outing with a homer, has bolstered Milwaukee's lineup alongside William Contreras and Brice Turang. Logan Henderson's 9-2 record and 2.48 ERA set up a clear edge against Kevin Gausman's 4.52 ERA in the probable matchup. Chicago's offense has shown pop with league-leading home runs but has dropped six of eight amid bullpen inconsistencies and absences like Dansby Swanson's oblique strain. The Cubs' home stand at Wrigley offers limited counter to Milwaukee's road strength and momentum entering the late-season stretch.
